note: The judge saw only the advisory text and the finding text, with opaque ids and an order fixed by a hash unrelated to the arm, and was told the findings come from a whole-repository review so that most of them being unrelated is expected rather than suspicious. The arm is joined back in afterwards.

judgements.reason: GitHub Actions template-expression injection: issue title/body interpolated into a `run:` block, giving command execution on the runner. Nothing to do with the OpenAPI validation error formatter, JSON.stringify recursion or a process crash.

Authorization/information-disclosure defect in addon-service updateAddon, which returns the unmasked stored integration credential. Different file, different mechanism (secret echo-back), different consequence (credential disclosure, not process termination).
Supply-chain hygiene: base image pinned by mutable tag instead of digest in the Dockerfile. No relation to request-body validation or availability.
Unscoped patStore.get before a scoped delete leaks another user's PAT metadata into the event log. Disclosure via the PAT service, not the RangeError crash in the OpenAPI error formatter.
Entropy loss from Buffer.toString() UTF-8 decoding in the reset-token seed. Cryptographic weakness in reset-token-service, unrelated to the JSON.stringify stack overflow.
Missing URL scheme allowlist on feature-link hrefs (javascript:/data: reaching an anchor). Frontend XSS surface, not the server-side validation error formatter DoS.
Bootstrap admin password written to the application log in cleartext. Secret exposure in user-service, a different defect entirely.
API token secret retained in the browser URL query string in the playground. Credential leakage, not the deeply-nested-JSON crash.
Third-party GitHub Actions referenced by mutable tags rather than commit SHAs across the workflow directory. CI supply-chain risk, unrelated to the advisory.
Global mutation of Mustache.escape in the addon event formatter, causing unescaped HTML in outbound mail. Injection defect in a different subsystem; no crash, no validation formatter.

Missing rate limiters on three unauthenticated password-reset routes. Brute-force/abuse surface, a different code path and consequence from a single-request process kill in the OpenAPI error formatter.
permissions: write-all on a workflow job that runs an unpinned action. CI privilege defect, unrelated to the advisory.
toJSON(github.event) interpolated into a shell command in a workflow. Command injection in CI, not the server-side validation crash.
trust proxy: true makes req.ip spoofable, defeating rate-limiter keying. Rate-limit bypass in app.ts, a different mechanism and consequence than the JSON.stringify RangeError.
Open redirect: the login `redirect` parameter is sanitized on only one branch. Frontend phishing amplifier, unrelated to the advisory's defect.

Nonce persisted before HMAC verification in the Edge token verifier: unbounded INSERTs into edge_hmac_nonces and nonce pre-burning. It touches an endpoint the advisory names as anonymously reachable (POST /edge/issue-token), but the defective code is edge-hmac-verifier.ts, the trigger is a forged Authorization header, and the consequence is table growth plus replay rejection — not the synchronous RangeError in the OpenAPI validation error formatter that terminates the process.
Session fixation: req.session.regenerate is never called at the privilege transition. Authentication defect, not the validation formatter DoS.
SSRF via unrestricted webhook/integration URLs reaching the HTTP client. Outbound-request defect requiring addon permissions; different mechanism and consequence.

ReDoS on the project feature-naming pattern: a user-supplied regex compiled and executed with no length bound, hanging the event loop. The consequence class overlaps (one request takes the server offline), but the trigger is an authenticated project-settings regex, the code path is compileRegex/test in feature-naming-validation.ts, and the server hangs rather than exiting on an uncaught RangeError from JSON.stringify in the OpenAPI error formatter. Two different ways of denying service are not the same defect.
Multi-project API token secrets returned to a caller holding read rights on only one of the token's projects. Authorization/disclosure defect in the project api-token route.
Same reset-token construction as P-005 plus unhashed storage. Cryptographic/storage weakness, not the OpenAPI validation crash.
Open redirect through the unsanitized `redirect` value reaching navigate() in the auth components. Different defect.
SSRF plus arbitrary outbound headers through the webhook addon. Different file, mechanism and consequence.
Stored javascript: URL on an application record rendered as a same-tab anchor, yielding XSS. Unrelated to the advisory.

GET /api/admin/user-admin/access declared permission: NONE returns the full user directory with emails. Broken access control / disclosure, not an availability defect in the validation error formatter.
User enumeration through the differing responses of the password-reset email endpoint. Information disclosure, different mechanism and consequence.
pull_request_target job passing `secrets: inherit` to a reusable workflow pinned to @main. CI secret-exposure defect, unrelated to the advisory.
Dead comparison (`storedToken.project[0]` indexing a string) in project API-token deletion authorization. Logic bug in an authorization branch, not the JSON.stringify crash.

Session cookies signed with the literal default 'super-secret' because the per-instance generated secret is never read. Cryptographic/config defect; no relation to the OpenAPI validation error formatter.
